title: Simplicial enriched Yoneda evaluation
statement:
Use simplicial sets and Kan complexes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and simplicial categories, enriched functors, mapping ends, projective simplicial model structures, and cofibrant-fibrant objects from [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] and [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. A simplicial functor preserves the identity vertices and simplicial composition; an enriched natural transformation is a family of vertex components satisfying the naturality equality on every mapping simplicial set.

Let $A$ be a small locally Kan simplicial category and let $\mathsf M=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$ have its projective simplicial model structure.  For $a\in A$, put $Y_a=A(-,a)$.  For every projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagram $P$, restriction at the enriched identity defines a simplicial isomorphism
\[
\varepsilon_{a,P}:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathsf M}(Y_a,P)\xrightarrow{\;\cong\;}P(a),
\qquad
\alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a(1_a).
\]
Its inverse sends a simplex $p$ of $P(a)$ to the enriched transformation $f\mapsto P(f)(p)$.  These maps are natural in $a$ and $P$ on the full simplicial mapping complexes, preserve all faces and degeneracies, and satisfy the enriched composition and unit equalities.

source.place: Explicit strict enriched Yoneda construction for simplicial categories, as used with the projective model of HTT Appendix A.3.3 in HTT Section 5.1.3; not a verbatim theorem of HTT.

proof.text: Put $I=A^{\mathrm{op}}$. The Kan-model clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] supplies a combinatorial simplicial model category of simplicial sets. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] with this target and the small simplicial category $I$: it gives the stated projective structure, objectwise tensors, and the enriched-end mapping object. Its free-diagram formula at $a$ and $\Delta^0$ gives $I(a,-)\times\Delta^0=Y_a$. Fix the cofibrant-fibrant $P$ in the statement and write $E_{a,P}=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathsf M}(Y_a,P)$. We compute this end directly. All object sets, simplices and ends lie in the containing universe specified by the cited nodes.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5: enriched projective model and free diagrams.

proof.text:
Write $\mu^P_{y,x}:A(y,x)\times P(x)\to P(y)$ for the enriched presheaf action. By the mapping-end description, an $n$-simplex $\alpha\in E_{a,P,n}$ is a family of simplicial maps $\alpha_x:A(x,a)\times\Delta^n\to P(x)$ satisfying
$$\alpha_{y,m}(f\circ g,t)=\mu^P_{y,x,m}(g,\alpha_{x,m}(f,t))$$
for every $m$, $g\in A(y,x)_m$, $f\in A(x,a)_m$ and $t:[m]\to[n]$. This is the defining enriched naturality equation, written on all mapping simplices. Let $1_a^m$ be the constant $m$-simplex at the identity and set $\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=\alpha_{a,n}(1_a^n,\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$. For $\rho:[k]\to[n]$, simpliciality of $\alpha_a$ gives
$$\rho^*\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=\alpha_{a,k}(1_a^k,\rho)=\varepsilon_k(\rho^*\alpha).$$
Thus evaluation is a simplicial map.

source.place: Section 5.1.3 opening paragraph: agent expansion of evaluation in the usual enriched Yoneda argument, with all simplicial parameters.

proof.text:
For $p\in P(a)_n$ define the $x$-component of $\eta_n(p)$ on $m$-simplices by
$$\eta_n(p)_{x,m}(f,t)=\mu^P_{x,a,m}(f,t^*p).$$
The action map is simplicial, so these component formulas commute with each operator $\sigma:[\ell]\to[m]$: both sides become $\mu^P_{x,a,\ell}(\sigma^*f,(t\sigma)^*p)$. Associativity of the action gives
$$\mu^P_{y,a}(f\circ g,t^*p)=\mu^P_{y,x}(g,\mu^P_{x,a}(f,t^*p)),$$
which is exactly the end equation from step 2. Hence the family is an $n$-simplex of $E_{a,P}$. Replacing $p$ by $\rho^*p$ replaces $t^*p$ by $(\rho t)^*p$, which also describes restriction of that end simplex. Therefore $\eta:P(a)\to E_{a,P}$ is simplicial.

source.place: Section 5.1.3 opening paragraph: agent expansion of the inverse using the presheaf action.

proof.text:
The identity action gives $\varepsilon_n\eta_n(p)=\mu^P_{a,a,n}(1_a^n,p)=p$. Conversely, the end equation of step 2 with $f=1_a^m$ and $g=h\in A(x,a)_m$ gives
$$\alpha_{x,m}(h,t)=\mu^P_{x,a,m}(h,\alpha_{a,m}(1_a^m,t)).$$
Simpliciality gives $\alpha_{a,m}(1_a^m,t)=t^*\varepsilon_n(\alpha)$, so the right side is $\eta_n(\varepsilon_n(\alpha))_{x,m}(h,t)$. This holds for every $x,m,h,t$, and the end is a subobject of the product of its component function simplicial sets; thus $\eta_n\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=\alpha$. Together with the operator checks, this proves the claimed simplicial isomorphism.

source.place: Section 5.1.3 opening paragraph: agent expansion of the two inverse identities.

proof.text:
Check enriched naturality in the presheaf variable on arbitrary $r$-simplices. Let $\theta\in\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathsf M}(P,Q)_r$ and $\alpha\in E_{a,P,r}$, so $\theta_x:P(x)\times\Delta^r\to Q(x)$. Using the diagonal on the common parameter, their enriched composite has components
$$(\theta\star\alpha)_{x,m}(h,t)=\theta_{x,m}(\alpha_{x,m}(h,t),t).$$
Evaluation therefore gives
$$\varepsilon_r(\theta\star\alpha)=\theta_{a,r}(\varepsilon_r(\alpha),\mathrm{id}_{[r]}).$$
This is equality on every degree of the two simplicial maps $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(P,Q)\times E_{a,P}\to Q(a)$, hence enriched naturality in $P$. Applying the inverse identities of step 4 to this equality gives naturality of $\eta$ as well. The identity transformation acts by $p\mapsto p$. For another parameterized transformation $\phi:Q\to R$, evaluation of $(\phi\star\theta)\star\alpha$ is $\phi_a(\theta_a(\varepsilon\alpha,t),t)$, equal to evaluation of $\phi\star(\theta\star\alpha)$ by the displayed formula. This verifies units and composition in this variable on the full mapping complexes.

source.place: Section 5.1.3 opening paragraph: agent expansion of enriched naturality, units and composition in the presheaf variable.

proof.text:
For enriched naturality in $a$, take any $r$-simplex $u\in A(a',a)_r$ and $\alpha\in E_{a,P,r}$. The parameterized map $Y(u):Y_{a'}\times\Delta^r\to Y_a$ has components $(h,t)\mapsto t^*u\circ h$. The diagonal-parameter composite $\beta=\alpha\star Y(u)$ thus has $\beta_{x,m}(h,t)=\alpha_{x,m}(t^*u\circ h,t)$. Evaluation and the end equation from step 2 give
$$\varepsilon_{a',P,r}(\beta)=\alpha_{a',r}(u,\mathrm{id}_{[r]})=\mu^P_{a',a,r}(u,\varepsilon_{a,P,r}(\alpha)).$$
This proves equality of the simplicial maps $A(a',a)\times E_{a,P}\to P(a')$ in every degree, including their operators. The inverse identities of step 4 give the corresponding equality for $\eta$. For $v\in A(a'',a')_r$ and $p\in P(a)_r$, the presheaf law reads
$$\mu^P_{a'',a,r}(u\circ v,p)=\mu^P_{a'',a',r}(v,\mu^P_{a',a,r}(u,p));\qquad \mu^P_{a,a,r}(1_a^r,p)=p.$$
These are exactly the composition and unit equalities after evaluation; the maps $Y(u)$ obey them by associative unital composition in $A$. Finally the end equation for $\theta:P\to Q$ gives $\theta_{a',r}(\mu^P(u,p),\mathrm{id})=\mu^Q(u,\theta_{a,r}(p,\mathrm{id}))$, so the two variable actions commute. Hence the isomorphisms and their inverses are enriched natural on $A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathsf M$ with every stated compatibility.

source.place: Section 5.1.3 opening paragraph: agent expansion of enriched naturality, units and composition in the representing variable, and commutation of the two actions.

lean.statement: theorem enriched_yoneda_evaluation (hA : ∀ a b : A, SSet.KanComplex (sHom a b)) (E : SimplicialDiagramEnrichment Aᵒᵖ SSet.{u}) (T : SimplicialTensorCotensor SSet.{u}) [@ProjectiveSimplicialModelStructure _ _ _ _ _ kanModel _ T E] : ∃ ε : ∀ (a : A) (P : SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif E.Diagrams), sHom (representableObject E a) P.obj ≅ (SimplicialDiagramEnrichment.value P.obj).obj (op a), (∀ (a : A) (P : SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif E.Diagrams), (ε a P).hom = evaluation E a P.obj) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (P : SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif E.Diagrams) (x : Aᵒᵖ), (𝟙 _ ⊗ₘ (ε a P).inv) ≫ componentApplication E (representableObject E a) P.obj x = (β_ _ _).hom ≫ uncurry ((SimplicialDiagramEnrichment.value P.obj).map (op a) x)) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (P Q : SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif E.Diagrams), eComp SSet (representableObject E a) P.obj Q.obj ≫ (ε a Q).hom = ((ε a P).hom ⊗ₘ 𝟙 (sHom P.obj Q.obj)) ≫ componentApplication E P.obj Q.obj (op a)) ∧ (∀ (a' a : A) (P : SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif E.Diagrams), (postcomposition E a' a ⊗ₘ 𝟙 _) ≫ eComp SSet (representableObject E a') (representableObject E a) P.obj ≫ (ε a' P).hom = (𝟙 _ ⊗ₘ (ε a P).hom) ≫ (β_ _ _).hom ≫ uncurry ((SimplicialDiagramEnrichment.value P.obj).map (op a) (op a'))) ∧ (∀ a : A, eId SSet a ≫ postcomposition E a a = eId SSet (representableObject E a)) ∧ (∀ a b c : A, eComp SSet a b c ≫ postcomposition E a c = (postcomposition E a b ⊗ₘ postcomposition E b c) ≫ eComp SSet (representableObject E a) (representableObject E b) (representableObject E c))
lean.note: Uses the recorded SimplicialDiagramEnrichment and ProjectiveSimplicialModelStructure, including genuine graded-natural mapping ends and their composition. Helpers construct the representable, the enriched Yoneda map and evaluation by their full simplicial formulas. The inverse is characterized by its action on every end projection. The Kan model is extracted from the presheaf-model theorem whose three prescribed morphism classes determine its data uniquely; no diagram or arbitrary map is chosen.
